article.headline: San Francisco 49ers release wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk following contract saga
article.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are releasing wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk on Monday after over a year of negotiations.
article.body: The relationship between the San Francisco 49ers and wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has reached its conclusion as the team parts ways with the former first-round pick. This decision brings an end to a standoff that persisted for more than a year, officially shifting the status of the receiver to free agency. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the move on Monday, noting that the team is finalizing the release immediately following their Sunday Night Football victory. The release grants Aiyuk the freedom to sign with any other team in the league. For the 49ers, the move follows other front office adjustments made just before their Week 11 win. While the team moves on from their former standout, the professional future of the wide receiver remains a subject of intense speculation across the NFL. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, the Washington Commanders are currently considered the most likely landing spot for the wide receiver. The logistics of the release are now being processed, allowing Aiyuk to explore his options in the open market. As a former first-round draft choice, Aiyuk's sudden availability changes the roster dynamics for multiple franchises looking to bolster their offensive production mid-season. Teams now have the opportunity to negotiate directly with Aiyuk to incorporate him into their offensive schemes for the remainder of the current campaign. The organization has not provided further statements regarding the specific terms of the departure, focusing instead on the team's ongoing progress after their latest result. Further updates regarding his signing will depend on official negotiations with potential new clubs.

news.title: Al-Ittihad to Host Uzbekistan's Pakhtakor in AFC Champions League Elite Tomorrow
news.og_title: Al-Ittihad to Host Uzbekistan's Pakhtakor in AFC Champions League Elite Tomorrow
news.og_desc:
Jeddah, November 22, 2026, SPA -- Saudi Arabia's Al-Ittihad will host Uzbekistan's Pakhtakor tomorrow at King Abdullah Sports City Stadium in Jeddah in the fifth round of the West Region league stage of the 2026–2027 AFC Champions League Elite.
    Al-Ittihad will seek to return to winning ways and strengthen its chances of advancing to the next round, drawing confidence from its favorable record against Pakhtakor. The two sides have met four times, with Al-Ittihad remaining unbeaten and winning three of those encounters. The Jeddah-based side will also look to secure its first home win in this season's competition after losing both previous home matches.
    The match comes at a crucial stage for Al-Ittihad, which needs all three points after suffering a 4–1 defeat to the UAE's Al-Ain. With four points, the team currently sits 10th in the standings and needs positive results in its remaining matches to improve its chances of reaching the round of 16.
    Pakhtakor, meanwhile, has two points and will be looking to improve its position. However, the Uzbek side faces a difficult away challenge, having failed to win any of its last six away matches in the AFC Champions League Elite, recording three draws and three defeats.
    Al-Ain currently leads the West Region standings with 12 points, followed by Al-Hilal, Esteghlal, and Shabab Al-Ahli, each with nine points. Al-Qadsiah and Saudi Arabia's Al-Ahli have eight points apiece, while Al-Nassr has six points from three matches.
    Al-Shamal follows with five points, while Neftchi and Al-Ittihad have four points each. Al-Wasl and Air Force SC have three points apiece, followed by Tractor, Pakhtakor, and Al-Sadd with two points each. Al-Gharafa remains without a point.
    -- SPA
21:03 Local Time 18:03 GMT

news.title: Al-Ittihad Coach Eyes Victory over Pakhtakor to Make Up for Previous Result
news.og_title: Al-Ittihad Coach Eyes Victory over Pakhtakor to Make Up for Previous Result
news.og_desc:
Jeddah, November 22, 2026, SPA -- Al-Ittihad's German head coach Jens Wissing confirmed his team's readiness to face Uzbekistan's Pakhtakor tomorrow at King Abdullah Sports City Stadium in Jeddah in the fifth round of the 2026–2027 AFC Champions League Elite. He expressed his determination to secure victory by capitalizing on home advantage and the support of the fans.
    Speaking at a press conference held today at Al-Ittihad Club, Wissing said the team aims to deliver a better performance and make up for its showing in the previous match. He described tomorrow's encounter as an opportunity to achieve a positive result in front of its supporters.
    He noted that the recent international break provided an opportunity to improve the players' readiness and restore their confidence. He stressed that the team must now focus on upcoming matches and what it can achieve moving forward.
    Wissing acknowledged that Al-Ittihad had collected just four points from a possible 12 in its previous matches, falling short of fans' expectations. However, he emphasized that the work undertaken over the past five months had contributed to the team's development and helped it produce strong performances despite disappointing results in some matches.
    He added that the coaching staff understands the team's capabilities and what it can deliver on the pitch. The staff is working to secure victories while taking a realistic approach to the current situation.
    Regarding the transfer window, Wissing explained that clubs always seek to strengthen their squads according to their needs. However, he confirmed that he had not requested any new signings, as the team already has players with the necessary capabilities. He also described his relationship with everyone at the club as positive, noting that all are committed to delivering their best.
    For his part, Al-Ittihad player Saad Al-Mousa expressed the players' determination to achieve a positive result against Pakhtakor. He acknowledged that some players would be unavailable but stressed that the remaining squad members are capable of delivering the expected performance.
    Al-Mousa said the team had used the break to address defensive errors. He expressed confidence in the team's defenders and emphasized that work is ongoing to correct mistakes and prevent them from recurring in upcoming matches.
    -- SPA
20:23 Local Time 17:23 GMT
